messages:
ross: Filing follow-up from yesterday's PM. Posting the condensed checklist so we can turn this into a tiny sprint board. Link to postmortem: https://redwood/reports/stream-postmortem-19149 :clipboard:
priya: thanks — I'll take the reconnect/backoff changes. plan: add idempotent handshake token + exp backoff, default 3 retries. target: 2026-04-02.
mike: I can own the partial-response detection + metrics. will add a Prom rule and a dashboard panel. downtimes historically spike at ~30s, so threshold = two partials within 60s.
nada (typo, corrected): sorry, meant ada: @mike can you add a sample alert query?
mike: yea, will paste draft here once done.
nada (typo again): ignore previous, ada: I’ll run a quick load test for the new handshake on staging after Priya’s PR merges. ETA: 2 days.
ross: Priya — include a small compatibility matrix: clients with older protocols should fallback to simple non-streaming behavior. list the affected SDKs.
priya: noted. SDKs: node-sdk v1.*, python-sdk <=0.9. I’ll add a feature flag to gate the new handshake.
sophie: for the reconnect logic, we discussed maintaining a small local buffer to re-send missed tokens on reconnect. is that still the plan?
priya: yes. implementation notes: preserve last acked seq, resume from seq+1. store last 128 tokens in-memory per connection. fallback to full re-request if seq mismatch.
casey: quick ops ask — can we get a temporary rate-limited fallback to the smaller model when streaming failures exceed 5% for 10m? That would reduce user impact.
ross: good ops mitigation. @engbot can we get an automated route that switches to 'cheaper-legacy' model if error rate > 5% for 10m?
engbot: /action created: route-fallback-runbook (owner: infra-rotations) — scheduled check every 60s, TTL 30m.
nada (typo again): sorry, ada: I'll coordinate with infra for the fallback route test.
ada: ugh — stop the typos, ada here.
ada: also adding a small client-side improvement: expose a reconnect callback and let app retry with linear backoff up to 6s.
priya: config snippet I’ll use for server backoff: ```json
{"retries":3,"backoff_ms":[200,800,3200],"handshake_token_ttl_s":60}```
casey: can we standardize on an ISO date for due dates in tasks? helps integrations.
ross: yes — use YYYY-MM-DD. I'll convert current dates.
priya: action items summary (short): 1) Priya: handshake+backoff PR (due 2026-04-02). 2) Mike: partial-response alerts + dashboard (due 2026-03-30). 3) Ada: staging load tests (due 2026-03-29). 4) Casey/infra: model-fallback route test (due 2026-03-31). 5) Sophie: client reconnect callback docs (due 2026-03-28).
sophie: I'll add docs + small example in node and python.
ross: tagging owners into the incident tracker. please update the tracker row with status: todo/in-progress/done as you go.
priya: will open PR and ping for review when ready.
mike: draft alert query for partial responses (promQL): `sum(rate(chat_stream_partial_responses_total[5m])) / sum(rate(chat_stream_requests_total[5m])) > 0.05` — will tune after test.
ada: noticed one recurring pattern in the PM: long GC spikes + client slowdowns around hot nodes. I propose a short-term: enable jemalloc on those nodes and schedule a GC tuning pass.
casey: agree. infra will add jemalloc flag to the runtime image, test in canary.
ross: excellent. can everyone drop a one-liner in the tracker when done? I'll do a sync on Mon to verify closure.
priya: one-liner for tracker: "handshake/backoff PR opened — refs #1234 — in review".
mike: tracker: "alerts + dash added — pending threshold validation".
ada: tracker: "staging load tests passed 3/3 — no regressions".
sophie: tracker: "client docs + examples merged".
casey: tracker: "fallback route tested in canary — passed".
ross: thanks all. if anyone hits blockers, post here and I’ll escalate. :thumbsup:
